children: "We've got to come to terms with the cost side and inflation side failure on the (Fed's) mandate," Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said Monday.
"The employment and growth side are both remarkably stable," he said in a moderated discussion at a Leadership Greater Chicago event. "The big problem has all been on the inflation side."
Whenever he visits businesses in the Chicago Fed's district, Goolsbee said, "All we hear about is affordability and costs."

That implies that the Federal Open Market Committee needs to continue raising rates, though he didn't say that explicitly. Traders have increased their expectations of a rate hike recently. The probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike at the Fed's December meeting rose to 84.5% on Monday, up from 76.3% on Friday, according to the CME FedWatch tool.
In central banks' standard playbook, policymakers are advised to look through supply shocks that produce a one-time price hike that fades over time.
"Supply shocks are supposed to go away," Goolbee said. "What we're grappling with is why hasn't it gone away sooner?"
Data center investment is starting to look like “old-fashioned overheating” in demand, he added.
If the economy is overheating, the conventional wisdom is to get aggressive early in addressing that, Goolsbee noted.

title: Fed needs to 'come to terms' with inflation, Chicago Fed's Goolsbee says
